paper_metadata.title: BQ-Bank: A Quantum Software for Finance and Banking

experiments.description: Quantum option pricing for European-style call/put options using amplitude estimation, compared against Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo baselines.

algorithm.ansatz: parameterized quantum circuits for loading the underlying asset distribution

hyperparameters.n: number of qubits used in the user interface
hyperparameters.2n: Monte Carlo sampling number set equal to 2^n for comparison
hyperparameters.c: small constant used in the amplitude rotation approximation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Underlying asset expiration-date prices are discretized into probabilities p_i and encoded into an n-qubit state; an extra qubit marks whether payoff is nonzero; an ancillary qubit is rotated according to the encoded payoff.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate option price e^{-rT} E[f(S)] for European call/put options, with call payoff f(S_T)=max(0,S_T-K) and put payoff given by Black-Scholes-style payoff definition.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints; payoff is encoded via amplitude rotation and estimated with QAE.

problem_instance.description: A user-selected European-style option pricing instance entered through the BQ-Bank interface.

dataset_specification.description: Inputs include current underlying price, option valid period, risk-free rate, annualized volatility, exercise price, and call/put choice. No fixed ticker/date range is reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Expiration-date price distribution is assumed under random-walk theory, sampled and discretized into probabilities p_i.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single illustrative example shown in Figure 2; results compared with Black-Scholes and Monte Carlo.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Discretize the underlying asset distribution and compute payoff samples for comparison baselines.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated expected payoff to present value using e^{-rT}.

speedup_claims.conditions: For option pricing via quantum amplitude estimation; precision scales as O(M^-1) versus O(M^-1/2) for Monte Carlo.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents a single illustrative example and notes run-to-run randomness; no wall-clock timing or resource counts are reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup claimed via QAE; precision O(M^-1)

experiments.description: Quantum Value at Risk estimation using amplitude estimation, compared against historical VaR, parametric VaR, and Monte Carlo VaR baselines.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A discretized random variable X is mapped to an m-qubit basis state |i> with probabilities p_i; an ancillary qubit is flipped according to a threshold function f(i) that is 1 for i<=k and 0 otherwise.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_alpha(X) = -inf{x in R : F_X(x) > alpha} by finding the threshold k such that cumulative probability up to k reaches alpha.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Thresholding via the function f(i) and QAE probability estimation; no penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: VaR example with a normal distribution model, 0.95 confidence, 30 holding days, and a portfolio of two assets.

dataset_specification.description: Assets are China Bao An and Ping An Bank, with 10 units of each purchased. The paper does not provide a date range or exact historical dataset.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical returns are summarized by mean and standard deviation for the parametric and Monte Carlo baselines; the quantum method discretizes the random variable into M states.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Results are shown across multiple sampling points (1 to 512) and compared to H-VaR, P-VaR, and MC-VaR.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Historical VaR; Parametric VaR; Monte Carlo VaR
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute historical mean/variance for P-VaR and simulate geometric Brownian motion for MC-VaR.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Extract VaR from sorted historical losses or from the estimated distribution quantile.

speedup_claims.conditions: Quantum amplitude estimation for VaR estimation; precision O(M^-1) compared with classical MC-VaR precision O(M^-1/2).
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports convergence behavior across sampling points but does not provide runtime or qubit counts.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization using a hybrid QAOA plus classical optimization workflow on a constrained asset-selection instance.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate classical-quantum loop until the objective approximately reaches a minimum

hyperparameters.b: investment budget / number of assets to purchase
hyperparameters.p: QAOA depth (number of layers), not numerically specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary decision variables x_i indicate whether each asset is purchased; mapping x_i -> (I - sigma_z_i)/2 converts the objective to an Ising Hamiltonian.
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_{x in {0,1}^n} q x^T C x - mu^T x subject to 1^T x = b
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Budget constraint enforced by a quadratic penalty term A(b - sum_i x_i)^2; assets with minx > 0 are fixed into a mandatory set X1, remaining assets are selected by QAOA from X2.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_C = C(sigma_z_1, sigma_z_2, ..., sigma_z_n); loss Hamiltonian includes q sum_{i,j} C_{ji} x_i x_j - sum_i x_i mu_i + A(b - sum_i x_i)^2

problem_instance.description: A portfolio optimization example shown in Figures 8 and 9 with preset assets and historical return curves.

dataset_specification.description: User provides candidate assets, preferred min/max shares, budget b, risk factor q, and historical period [t_i, t_f]. Figure 9 shows an example portfolio with three selected assets and a return curve, but the paper does not name the assets.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Assets with minx > 0 are assigned to a fixed purchase set X1; remaining assets are optimized over with QAOA; final proportions are refined with trust-constr.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single illustrative example; result shown as optimal portfolio diagram and historical return curve.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Partition assets into mandatory and optimizable sets based on minx; construct Hamiltonian from the QUBO/Ising mapping.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use trust-constr to compute final asset proportions after QAOA selects the asset subset.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper describes a hybrid QAOA plus classical workflow and shows a single illustrative example, but does not report quantitative performance metrics, approximation ratios, or runtime comparisons.
